title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: in the 4th draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck axiomatises a 'magasin' (M, ≤, ≪̊, |o|). M is a set of figures or regions. ≤ is inclusion. X ≪̊ Y means 'X lies in the interior of Y'. X |o| Y is a disjointness or 'strangeness' relation (for lines it is parallelism, ∥). Axioms Mag 1–Mag 4 are on p. 22–24. On the previous page he embeds M into its elementary figures Figél(M) via X ↦ Mutilations(X) ('Multiomb'). Then |Mutilations(X)| = Ombre(X) = {M ≪ X} and its interior is Ombre°(X) = {M ≪̊ X}. He asks whether this embedding, already compatible with ≤, ≪ and the non-disjointness relation, is compatible with |o|.

This page:
(1) Multiomb(X) |o| Multiomb(Y) ⇔ Omb°(X) ∩ Omb°(Y) = ∅ ⇔ there is no Z ∈ M with Z ≪̊ X and Z ≪̊ Y. That is, {X,Y} has no lower bound in (M, ≪̊).
(2) X |o| Y ⇒ Multiomb(X) |o| Multiomb(Y). Proof: suppose Z ≪̊ X and Z ≪̊ Y. Mag 3 b) (a compatibility of |o| with ≪̊) gives Z ≪̊ Z. This contradicts Mag 3 a) (irreflexivity of ≪̊ on non-empty objects).
(3) He asks about the converse: can |o| always be expressed through ≪̊ alone, by X|o|Y ⇔ {X,Y} not ≪̊-minorised? No. Take two distinct lines x, y ∈ L. Lines have empty interior, so nothing is ≪̊ both, and {x,y} is not minorised. Yet x |o| y (here x ∥ y) generally fails, since distinct lines meet. He adds that it fails 'even in general' for divisible regions.
(4) Conclusion: requiring that |o| be induced by ≪̊ is an extra hypothesis of 'quasi-set-theoretic' nature that involves no special condition on lines.

The next page takes this up. It axiomatises magasins (M, ≤, ≪̊) with |·| defined by non-minorisation. It obtains the hierarchy: general magasins ⊃ magasins (≤, ≪̊) ⊃ quasi-set-theoretic magasins ⊃ set-theoretic magasins.

Purpose: a point-free, order-theoretic foundation for tame plane topology or geometry ('figures', 'lines', 'regions'). Here he determines whether the contact or disjointness relation is definable from interior-inclusion.
errors: No genuine error. Step (2) depends on the precise form of Mag 3 a), b) (p. 22–24, not visible here); the argument is consistent with b) being of the form 'Z ≪̊ X, X |o| Y, Z ≪̊ Y ⇒ Z ≪̊ Z' or similar.
The counterexample with lines tacitly assumes that elements of L have empty ≪̊-interior (no non-empty Z ≪̊ x). This is natural but not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures expressed as absence of a common interior minorant: Omb°(X) ∩ Omb°(Y) = ∅ ⇔ {X,Y} not minorised for ≪̊
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology: 'no common interior part' / non-overlap of interiors (cf. Whitehead–Clarke connection structures; RCC relations DC/EC versus overlap via NTPP)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992); contact algebras (Dimov–Vakarelov 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Not in his published texts; the tame-topology programme is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6.

ideas.what: Observation that in a domain containing lower-dimensional objects (lines), disjointness is not definable from interior inclusion; definability is an extra 'quasi-set-theoretic' axiom
ideas.modern_name: Failure of regularity / definability of contact from the part relation in mixed-dimensional mereotopology (multi-dimensional mereotopology, e.g. Galton; Gotts' INCH calculus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Galton (1996, 2004), Gotts (1996), Pratt-Hartmann (2007) on mixed-dimension regions

ideas.what: Hierarchy of 'magasins': general (≤, ≪̊, |o|) ⊃ (≤, ≪̊) with |o| defined ⊃ quasi-set-theoretic ⊃ set-theoretic (developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic hierarchy of point-free (pointless) topological structures, akin to contact algebras and proximity lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Vries (1962) compingent algebras; Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras; Düntsch–Winter

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'magasins' are an independent axiomatisation of point-free mereotopology with mixed dimensions (regions and lines). That field was developed separately in philosophy, AI and qualitative spatial reasoning (RCC, contact algebras), and the two are not linked in the literature. This page isolates exactly the RCC-style question of whether 'disconnected' is definable from 'non-tangential part'. It shows the answer fails when lower-dimensional elements are present.
missed.quote: Mais notons que si x, y ∈ L, x ≠ y, alors {x,y} n'est pas minoré dans M pour ≪̊, mais on n'a pas pour autant x |o| y i.e. x ∥ y !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It provides a Grothendieck-designed foundation for tame or semi-algebraic plane geometry ('topologie modérée') phrased as point-free order structures. Comparing it with contact algebras and mixed-dimension mereotopology could give a reference axiomatics for o-minimal-style figure geometry.

missed.claim: The status of |o| for 'divisible regions', where he says the characterisation by ≪̊ fails even in general, is left unanalysed. It is also unclear which magasins arising from tame plane geometry satisfy the quasi-set-theoretic axiom.
missed.quote: Donc le fait que |o| soit induit par ≪̊ s'[énonce] : une hypothèse de nature "quasi-ensembliste", mais sans conditions particulières aux lignes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete classification question for point-free models of tame topology.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary order theory. Its interest is historical: an unpublished Grothendieck axiomatics of point-free plane topology, closely parallel to mereotopology and contact algebras, that the literature has not connected to him.
transcription_corrections: 'Mais l'inverse est-il [?]' is most likely 'Mais l'inverse est-il vrai ?'

The phrase 'X |o| Y peut-il s'exprimer toujours i.e. ≪̊ ?' reads as 'X |o| Y peut-il s'exprimer toujours en termes de la relation d'ordre ≪̊ ?'; the line 'en termes de la relation d'ordre' continues the question.
'(Même, en général, ... dans le cas des régions divisibles.)' probably reads '(Même, en général, faux dans le cas des régions divisibles.)'
'On a bien bien [?]' should be 'On a bien'.
Line 1: the deleted line is 'Multiomb(X) |o| Multiomb(Y) ⇔' and the margin word is 'donc'.
